sourceObjectiveEnglish: Separate now from tomorrow: Use a present form of ir + a + infinitive: voy a estudiar.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Dos momentos with a patient classmate. Practice separate now from tomorrow. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: Use a present form of ir + a + infinitive: voy a estudiar. This expresses a planned future action. Do not conjugate the second verb.

examples.en: Now I am reading at home.

cards.decisionNote: Spanish está marks condition/location; French est also marks identity. A context-free scored equivalent hides that contrast.
Spanish el is masculine singular; French le/l’ depends on the following sound and noun.
Spanish la groups feminine article, object it and person her; French requires role, gender and elision in context.
Spanish un and French un depend on the noun; a universal face needs dictionary context.
Spanish en groups in/on/at; French à, dans and sur differ by phrase.
Amigos may be mixed-gender friends; French amis/amies requires group context.
Spanish de groups of/from; French de/du/des/d’ depends on phrase and contraction.
Spanish estoy is condition/location or part of an ongoing-action construction; French suis versus a present-tense verb or être en train de needs context.

cards.sourceEnglish: Now I am reading at home.
cards.proposedFrench: En ce moment, je lis à la maison.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish estoy leyendo is progressive; ordinary French present plus en ce moment expresses ongoing action. Qualified review may prefer être en train de lire.

cards.proposedFrench: Julia prépare le dîner en ce moment.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish está preparando is progressive; candidate French present plus en ce moment preserves ongoing time without a mechanical auxiliary calque.

cards.sourceSpanish: Mañana vamos a visitar a Diego.
cards.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow we are going to visit Diego.
cards.proposedFrench: Demain, nous allons rendre visite à Diego.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish visitar a Diego has personal a; French rendre visite à Diego uses a governed preposition. Decide visit/rendre visite and register in context.

cards.sourceSpanish: Después va a comprar un libro.
cards.sourceEnglish: Afterward he is going to buy a book.
cards.proposedFrench: Après, il va acheter un livre.

cards.sourceSpanish: Vamos a hablar después de la cena.
cards.sourceEnglish: We are going to talk after dinner.
cards.proposedFrench: Nous allons parler après le dîner.
cards.decisionNote: Source vamos a hablar is planned future; French aller + infinitive preserves the structure and must not be read as motion.

cards.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow I am going to study Spanish.
cards.decisionNote: Source Spanish-language object is español; French l’espagnol is the language, not a new curriculum target.

cards.sourceSpanish: Ana va a comprar un libro.
cards.sourceEnglish: Ana is going to buy a book.

reader.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow we are going to visit Diego.

reader.decisionNote: Keep the Diego visit and tomorrow time marker; Spanish personal a is not a route direction.

reader.sourceSpanish: Después va a comprar un libro.

reader.sourceSpanish: Vamos a hablar después de la cena.

reader.sourceEnglish: Tomorrow I am going to study Spanish.
reader.decisionNote: Study Spanish is the source meaning; do not silently change the object to French.

reader.sourceSpanish: Ana va a comprar un libro.
reader.sourceEnglish: Ana is going to buy a book.
We are going to eat at home.
reader.proposedFrench: Nous allons manger à la maison.

reader.sourceSpanish: Luis va a llamar a su hermano.
reader.sourceEnglish: Luis is going to call his brother.
reader.decisionNote: Spanish su brother resolves to Luis's brother in this scene; French son agrees with frère.

reader.sourceSpanish: Mis amigos van a visitar el museo.
reader.sourceEnglish: My friends are going to visit the museum.
reader.proposedFrench: Mes amis vont visiter le musée.
reader.decisionNote: Amigos may include more than male friends; choose amis/amies with scene context.

reader.sourceEnglish: Are you going to come to the library?
reader.proposedFrench: Est-ce que tu vas venir à la bibliothèque ?
reader.decisionNote: Source singular informal vas requires a French tu/register decision; candidate uses informal tu.

sourceDecisions: Qualified source and curriculum review must resolve the source objective's ir + a + infinitive alongside present progressive examples; preserve this now/planned-future contrast under the stable Master 16 identity.

Qualified French review must choose ordinary present versus être en train de for ongoing action, and aller + infinitive for future plans; teach the chosen forms directly without a literal Spanish auxiliary calque.
Qualified dictionary review must resolve context-dependent está, estoy, el, la, en, de, amigos and possessive su senses before scoring or saved-item mapping.
The source includes no clinical vocabulary; do not invent a clinical scenario. Any later clinical term must be taught directly and checked for precise meaning.
